title: Opening world and campaign limits
intro: These rules apply to every selectable scenario. Choose the world players enter and the campaign end date.
worldQuestion: At the opening date, which world setting should the game use?

inherit.title: Use the original or base mod world setting
inherit.description: Best when your mod adds content or changes only part of an existing world.

own.title: Plan for my scenario world
own.description: Records your intent for an alternate world or special era. It does not rewrite history files automatically.

startDate.label: Scenario opening date
startDate.hint: Use the same date shown by the scenario players will choose.

endDate.label: Scenario end date
endDate.hint: A valid date later than every saved scenario becomes the campaign end date in HOI4.

compatibilityNotice: Your latest selectable scenario starts on or after the vanilla 1949 campaign end. Until you set a later scenario end date, the export adds a clearly reported compatibility end date so the game does not conclude immediately.

timelineBaseline.vanilla: Standalone project: the comparison baseline is vanilla HOI4 (campaign end: 1 January 1949).
timelineBaseline.unregistered: Base mod timeline: source not registered. The program will not assume that the base mod ends in 1949.
timelineBaseline.rawBookmarkCoverage: This panel uses scenarios saved in the workbench. Preserved raw Bookmark files are checked separately during export.

saveFailed: Could not save the scenario settings.
saveReadbackMismatch: Reading back did not return the values just saved. Nothing is marked as saved; try again.

ownWorldSummary.title: Your world-setting choice
ownWorldSummary.description: You want players to enter your scenario world. This setting records that choice only: review and author the required starting-world files yourself before release.

submodNotice: This project builds on a base mod whose timeline source is not registered. The program keeps the analysis read-only and will not automatically rewrite the base mod's world setting.

riskPreview.title: Opening world risk preview
riskPreview.inherit: You are keeping the original or base mod world setting. The program will only point out possible world-setting risks; it will not change that world for you.
riskPreview.unverified: Source not registered: there is no verified preview API for this world yet. The program will not pretend the result is known or change the world automatically.
riskPreview.verifiedIntro: The world setting can be verified. If you confirm this scenario setting, players will encounter these results:
riskPreview.verifiedEmpty: The world setting can be verified, but there are no player-facing changes to show yet. Check the scenario dates and world setting.

scenarioWorld.title: Players start in your scenario world
scenarioWorld.description: The opening world follows the setting you created for this scenario.

baseWorld.title: Base world changes stay out
baseWorld.description: Later world changes from the original game or base mod will not be applied automatically at the opening date.

campaignOpening.title: Campaign opening
campaignOpening.intro: Players can choose several scenarios, so HOI4 uses the earliest valid saved Bookmark as the campaign opening. Later Bookmarks remain selectable scenarios, not a new global opening.
campaignOpening.linked: This matches the earliest saved scenario, {bookmark}.
campaignOpening.unlinked: The earliest saved scenario starts on {date}. Sync the campaign opening before export.
campaignOpening.noValidBookmark: Save at least one Bookmark with a valid date before setting the campaign opening.
campaignOpening.workspaceIntro: These rules apply to every scenario. Edit each scenario's own date and country-selection presentation below.
